definitions.explanation: A sweet crystalline substance obtained from sugarcane or sugar beets, used as a sweetener in food and drinks.

examples.japanese: コーヒーに{砂糖|さとう}を{入|い}れますか。
examples.english: Do you put sugar in your coffee?

examples.japanese: {砂糖|さとう}をもう{少|すこ}しください。
examples.english: Please give me a little more sugar.

examples.japanese: このケーキには{砂糖|さとう}を{使|つか}いません。
{砂糖|さとう}と{塩|しお}を{間違|まちが}えないでください。
examples.english: Please don't confuse the sugar and salt.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}は{甘|あま}いものが{好|す}きなので、{砂糖|さとう}をたくさん{食|た}べたがりますが、{体|からだ}によくないです。
examples.english: Children like sweet things so they want to eat a lot of sugar, but it's not good for their bodies.

notes:
{砂糖|さとう} is sugar, one of the basic cooking ingredients in Japanese cuisine.

TYPES OF SUGAR:
- {白|しろ}{砂糖|さとう}: white sugar
- {黒|くろ}{砂糖|さとう}: brown sugar/muscovado
- グラニュー{糖|とう}: granulated sugar
- {角砂糖|かくざとう}: sugar cube

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {砂糖|さとう}を{入|い}れる: to add sugar
- {砂糖|さとう}{抜|ぬ}き: without sugar, sugar-free
- {砂糖|さとう}{控|ひか}えめ: low sugar

IN COOKING:
Unlike Western cooking, Japanese cuisine uses sugar in many savory dishes ({煮物|にもの}, teriyaki, etc.).

COMMON MISTAKE:
{砂糖|さとう} and {塩|しお} (salt) look similar - a common mix-up in the kitchen!

NOTE:
{佐藤|さとう} (same pronunciation) is one of the most common Japanese surnames.
